work_order.approach: Targeted fix on the PR branch, no rebuild. (1) In components/expense-editor.tsx, render the submit-row StateMessage only when there are no field errors (the same gate the top summary already uses), and suppress the payer/split LiveNote for a section the server just refused (errors.payers / errors.splits present), so each refusal sentence renders exactly once beside its field; pre-submit live advice is unchanged and DeleteExpenseForm keeps its StateMessage since it has no field-error path. (2) In lib/expenses/validation.ts add EXPENSE_UNCHANGED ('unchanged') and map it in expenseNoticeText to the existing no-change sentence; in lib/expenses/actions.ts redirect the unchanged edit path with that notice while the updated path keeps EXPENSE_UPDATED. The group page needs no edit because it renders expenseNoticeText generically. (3) Correct the existing unchanged-save test assertion to the unchanged URL and add the notice-mapping test; QA re-runs the T-15/T-16 specs against the two new criteria.

risks: FieldError carries no live-region role, so after dedupe the refusal is visible exactly once; a stricter screen-reader announcement audit is out of scope and QA T-16 counts visible text
DeleteExpenseForm keeps its StateMessage by design since it has no field-error path; no change there
work_order.root_cause: BUG-1: parseExpenseInput returns the shortfall sentence in two places by design (message plus fieldErrors.payers), and the editor renders it three times: the FieldError beside the payer rows, the client LiveNote recomputing the same paidPartsMessage, and the submit-row StateMessage rendering state.message unconditionally. Only the top summary is gated on empty fieldErrors, so every field-level refusal echoes twice plus the live-region third. BUG-2: updateExpense maps both the updated and the unchanged result kinds to the same EXPENSE_UPDATED notice param (validation.ts defines no unchanged notice value), so the redirect discards the Nothing-to-change message; worse, the existing unchanged-save test asserts the buggy ?expense=updated URL, which is why CI stayed green while the defect shipped.

cases: no-change save redirects to ?expense=unchanged and writes no activity row (corrects the existing assertion that locked in ?expense=updated)
changed save still redirects to ?expense=updated with a before/after feed row
expenseNoticeText maps the unchanged notice to the no-change sentence and still returns null for unknown values
shortfall parse returns the shortfall sentence as both message and fieldErrors.payers: the single-sentence contract the editor dedupe relies on

work_order.understanding: Attempt 1 (PR #20, plan v1) was architecturally right: 14 of 16 QA tests pass and every AC-1..AC-8 rollup passes. What it got wrong is two details in brand-new code, and its own test suite locked one of them in. First, components/expense-editor.tsx renders a refused shortfall sentence three times: the FieldError beside the payer rows, the client LiveNote recomputing the same paidPartsMessage, and the submit-row StateMessage rendering state.message unconditionally (only the top summary is gated on having no field errors). QA T-16 counts /short of/ 3x in main and the code has exactly these three render sites. Second, lib/expenses/actions.ts redirects both the updated and the unchanged edit paths to ?expense=updated so the Nothing-to-change message is unreachable, and lib/expenses/actions.test.ts asserts that buggy URL, which is why CI stayed green while QA documented BUG-2. Neither is a flaw in the v1 ledger design; both are small implementation errors with precise line-level fixes.

issue_snapshot.title: Expenses with all four split types, multi-payer and search
issue_snapshot.body:
Members can record who paid and how it splits with exact minor-unit math, the core ledger everything else derives from.

Person sees: expense editor (amount with currency display, description, date, single-or-multi payer picker with parts, four split-type tabs with per-member inputs for exact amounts, percentages or share counts and included or left out, live sum and shortfall line, category, note, Save) plus the newest-first expense list with filter and search. Contract: DEFINES lib/money calculators and the Expense, ExpensePayer and SplitLine writes together with the expense activity-writer rows (added, edited, deleted including the structured before and after), each create, edit and delete committing expense, payers, split lines and activity entry in one interactive transaction. Balances later read only stored payer parts and computed shares, never the inputs. Constraints: TR-4 minor units and remainder rule, TR-8 atomicity, human decisions to store the split rule and the before and after; no floats cross a module boundary.

**Risk.** Money and correctness risk: integer minor units end to end, four split calculators with remainder to first payer, stored inputs versus computed shares kept consistent, one interactive transaction per write that never half-writes.

**Out of scope**
- Balance simplification and settle-up payments
- Activity feed UI (expense activity rows are written now and displayed later)
- Receipts, recurring expenses and multi-currency groups (spec S-10 deferrals)

Covers: TR-3, TR-4, TR-8, TR-11
Part of #1.
Depends on #5.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Create expenses with description, amount, date, category and note as single or multi-payer where payer parts sum to the total, for equal, exact-amount, percentage and share splits
- **IAC-2** Validation names the shortfall and its size (for example parts sum to 450, 50 short of 500), the remainder goes to the first payer, and reopening an expense shows the stored split type and each input exactly as entered
- **IAC-3** Expense list is newest-first with member and category filter plus description search; edit and delete work for members, keep input on failed save, require a confirm naming the expense, and never half-write
- **IAC-4** Unit tests prove integer minor-unit math, sum preservation and remainder placement across generated splits for all four types, plus a failing write leaving no expense, payer, share or activity rows

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.

review.title: A no-change edit tells the user 'Expense updated.' although nothing was written.
review.detail:
A no-change edit tells the user 'Expense updated.' although nothing was written.

`lib/expenses/actions.ts:400`

Evidence: updateExpense returns redirectTo expenseNoticePath(..., EXPENSE_UPDATED) for both the 'updated' and 'unchanged' kinds (actions.ts:400-402); expenseNoticeText maps EXPENSE_UPDATED to 'Expense updated.', so the group page shows that for a no-op save while the 'Nothing to change.' state is discarded by the redirect.

Fix: When unchanged, return the success state with no redirectTo (the form is still on screen to show it), or add a distinct notice value for it.
